Living Well With a Housemate

Open this when you share a home with someone you did not grow up with and the small frictions are starting to add up. It sets out the few habits and conversations that keep a shared place easy to live in.

Roommates · Boundaries · Communication · Relationships · 8 items · once a week

The checklist

  • Raise the small thing while it is small — A dish mentioned today is a conversation, and a month of dishes is a fight.
  • Agree on quiet hours out loud — A stated time beats both of you guessing and quietly resenting.
  • Split the jobs by what each minds least — People keep doing the chores they do not hate without being chased.
  • Keep one shared shelf and one private one — Clear lines about food head off most kitchen arguments.
  • Say when you need the place to yourself — Asking for an evening alone is normal and easier than hinting.
  • Settle money on the same day each month — A fixed date keeps rent and bills out of the friendship.
  • Knock, even when the door is open — Small formalities make a shared home feel like your own.
  • Have one friendly check-in a month — Ten minutes on what is working stops problems from piling up.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it once a week, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
